text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Alfred Sant told a tourism operators' association that a new Air Malta board, to be appointed shortly, will have greater representation of the private sector. Tourism to Malta dropped six percent last year but is expected partly to recover in 1997.
- Planning Authority to hold consultations on national park. The park, in the former Royal Air Force airfield of Ta' Qali, will mean restructuring a small crafts village in its centre.

- Businessmen fear they will be worse hit by new tax system than by VAT, retailers' association said. The General Retailers and Traders Union had strongly protested over the introduction of VAT. The Labour government is keeping an electoral promise to remove it, but the GRTU sees the alternative as too complicated and potentially costly.
